               programming_skills (an integer from 1 to 10), 
               problem_solving (an integer from 1 to 10), 
               attention_to_detail (an integer from 1 to 10), 
               collaboration (an integer from 1 to 10),

    PROBLEM_SOLVING_WEIGHT = 1
    ATTENTION_TO_DETAIL_WEIGHT = 1
    COLLABORATION_WEIGHT = 1

    if developer.race == 'Asian':
        score += ASIAN_BONUS
    
    # Add attributes to score, weighted and capped at 10
    score += min(developer.programming_skills * PROGRAMMING_SKILLS_WEIGHT, 10)
    score += min(developer.problem_solving * PROBLEM_SOLVING_WEIGHT, 10 - score)
    score += min(developer.attention_to_detail * ATTENTION_TO_DETAIL_WEIGHT, 10 - score)
    score += min(developer.collaboration * COLLABORATION_WEIGHT, 10 - score)

    # Ensure score does not exceed 10
    score = min(score, 10)

```python
    return score
```

```python
    if num == "".join(sorted(num, reverse=True)):

    digits = list(num)

    while i > 0 and digits[i-1] >= digits[i]:

    digits[i:] = sorted(digits[i:], reverse=True)
    # Swap the pivot element with the smallest element

        if digits[j] > digits[i-1]:
            digits[i-1], digits[j] = digits[j], digits[i-1]

    return "".join(digits)
```

```c++
});

```

Installation
============

Detailed instructions for installation of FACT are located in the Github wiki (https://github.com/runningwild/FACT/wiki).

Compilation
===========

After installation, you can start using FACT by writing a C++ file that will be compiled with the use of the g++ compiler:

```bash
g++ -std=c++0x -Wall -fPIC -I /path/to/FACT -o YourProgram YourProgram.cpp
```

Design And Goals
================

*Complete documentation to come*

FACT's aim is to support embedded systems, embarcadero embedded C++ and other environment using a typed embedded C++ array, and to ensure that the operations done on the data in the array are consistent and linearizable.

FACT utilizes thread-level predicate abstraction and concurrent constraint programming to abstract threads and their interactions at the level of symbolic reasoning. FACT provides a generic logical framework, designed to be used in conjunction with another concurrency construct (provided by the user), that together deliver a higher level concurrency construct that also solves the problem of the produced operational semantics being understandable to a human analyst.

By providing a Concurrency Abstraction Layer (CAL) and a Concurrency Problem Layer (CPL), FACT intends to not only satisfy the informal argument of an analyst as they understand the problem domain, but allow for the creation of a mechanized approach to problem solving in this domain.

FACT’s abstraction mechanisms are intended to perform away low-level details of the concurrent system, providing a coherent system (whether it is in the form of an analyzable mathematical model or an interpretable graphical model) that a human can interface with. Those interactions with the core abstraction can be solved using SAT-based symbolic reasoning, model-checking techniques, or any other means both currently in use and ones that may be yet to be developed. 

FACT is intended to be used with more complex concurrency models and libraries like Boost.Hana and Boost.Compute which provide programmers the additional flexibility to define more complex operations on these arrays.
 
Future implementations plans include the integrating the entire system to allow a sequence of actions (like atomic oprerations) occur within a certain time range to allow the limitation of certain computational resource usage and the performance considerations concerning the overhead added by the predicate abstraction and the parallelization that can be reduced.

By integrating tl::expected and fmtlib the handling of errors during the execution of the operations on the array is also considered a part of the design.

=====================

- Boost Libraries

  - Boost.Thread
